- Working diagnosis (from transcript): Acute uncomplicated cystitis (urinary tract infection, bladder infection) suspected; three-day antibiotic therapy planned.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection)
  - Likelihood: High

- Urethritis due to sexually transmitted infection (Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Sexual activity with a new partner and dysuria; absence of discharge or cervicitis signs lowers probability but STI cannot be excluded.
- Pregnancy-related considerations (early pregnancy)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago with sexual activity; pregnancy test recommended if concern persists.
